verifications.claim: Retirement can begin as early as 62 for reduced social security benefits.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'The earliest a person can start receiving Social Security retirement benefits will remain at age 62.'; R8: 'Earliest age to collect Social Security retirement benefits; however, claiming before the full retirement age results in reduced monthly benefits.'; R10: 'You can start receiving your Social Security retirement benefits as early as age 62. However, you are entitled to full benefits only when you reach your full retirement age. If you start receiving benefits early, your benefits will be reduced'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state SS benefits can start at 62 with reduction.

verifications.claim: For those born in 1960 or later, full retirement age is 67.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'FRA will reach 67 for those born in 1960 or later'; R6: '1960 and later' [67]; R9: 'full retirement age, which would be 67 if you were born in 1960 or later'; R11: '1960 and later 67'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match across multiple SSA-related sources.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 65–66 for those born 1954 or earlier.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: '1943-1954' [66]; R8: 'born between 1943 and 1954, your full retirement age is 66'; R11: '1937 and prior 65'; '1943-54 66'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm FRA at 65 for pre-1938, increasing to 66 by 1943-1954, matching 65-66 range for 1954 or earlier.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 66 and 2–10 months for those born 1955–1959.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'born in 1959, FRA 66 and 10 months'; '1958, 66 and six months? [lists incrementally]'; R8: 'born between 1955 and 1959, full retirement age increases gradually by a few months'; R11: '1955 66 and 2 months'; '1956 66 and 4 months'... '1959 66 and 10 months'
verifications.reasoning: Precise incremental ages from 66+2 to 66+10 months exactly match birth years 1955-1959.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security is 67 for those born 1960 or later.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '67 for those born in 1960 or later'; R6: '1960 and later' [67]; R8: 'age 67 for people born in 1960 and later'; R9: 'age 67 if born in 1960 or later'; R11: '1960 and later 67'
verifications.reasoning: Direct and consistent statement across sources.

verifications.claim: Social Security benefits can start at 62 but are permanently reduced.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'benefits are reduced a fraction of a percent for each month before your full retirement age'; R8: 'claiming before the full retirement age results in reduced monthly benefits'; R10: 'If you start receiving benefits early, your benefits will be reduced a small percentage for each month before your full retirement age'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm start at 62 with permanent reduction for early claiming.

verifications.claim: Delayed retirement increases benefits by ~8% annually up to age 70.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'adding up to 8% for each full year you wait until age 70'; R5: 'eligible for delayed retirement credits that would increase your monthly benefit'; R8: 'earn credits that increase your monthly benefit by about eight percent for each year you delay applying, up to age 70'
verifications.reasoning: Exact ~8% per year up to 70 directly stated.

verifications.claim: Social Security replaces approximately 40% of the average wage earner's income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Social Security retirement benefits replace 40 percent of pre-retirement income for retirement beneficiaries'; R7: 'Social Security retirement benefits replace 40 percent of pre-retirement income'
verifications.reasoning: Precise 40% replacement rate for average earner directly quoted.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'automatically enrolled in Original Medicare... when you turn 65'; R8: 'Sign up for Medicare... [at] 65'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Medicare starts at age 65.

verifications.claim: People can work and receive benefits while retired.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Continuing to work while collecting Social Security'; R5: 'You can continue working and start receiving your retirement benefits'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported: work and receive SS benefits simultaneously.

verifications.claim: Benefits may be temporarily reduced if under full retirement age and earn over a certain limit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'temporarily withholds $1 of a worker's benefits for every $2 earned above $24,480... before full retirement age'; R5: 'benefits will be reduced if you earn more than the yearly earnings limits... recalculate your benefit amount to give you credit'; R8: 'if your earnings exceed a certain limit... retirement earnings test... reduced... recomputed to give you credit'
verifications.reasoning: Earnings test causes temporary reduction under FRA, with later recalculation.
